unit.why: A brief anecdote, quoted from the book Toldot Adam, in which the Besht opens a window and sees a great light over a dunghill from a tzaddik of centuries ago, followed by a short homiletic conclusion.

stories.start_quote: ובס׳ תולדות אדם רמזי פסח כ׳
stories.end_quote: ואין שום דבר יכול לכבותה עכ״ל
stories.summary_en: The Besht, while somewhere, opened a window and said he saw a great light over a dunghill, coming from a tzaddik of several hundred years earlier; the lesson drawn is that the holiness of Israel endures and cannot be extinguished.

quotes: ופתח החלון ואמר שרואה אור גדול
tags.why: The Besht sees a light that is invisible to others.

quotes: אור גדול מצדיק אחד מכמה מאות שנים
tags.why: A great light emanates from a long-dead tzaddik as a sign of his holiness.
He has a waking supernatural sight.

quotes: מזה אנו רואים שעצם קדושת ישראל קיימת
tags.why: The anecdote is quoted inside a homiletic frame that draws a lesson from it.

missing_concepts: holiness persisting in an impure place (dunghill)
